keyVerseText: And unto Eber were born two sons: the name of one was Peleg; for in his days was the earth divided; and his brother's name was Joktan. Peleg: that is Division
rootMeaning: The name יׇקְטָן (Yoqṭân) derives from the Hebrew root קָטֹן (qâṭôn), which means 'small' or 'insignificant.' This root conveys the sense of being made little or diminished, either literally or figuratively. The etymology 'he will be made little' suggests a foundational meaning of smallness or humility, which enriches the understanding of the name beyond a mere proper noun, highlighting a theme of diminishment or modest stature.
usageInScripture: The word Yoqṭân appears six times in Scripture, consistently as a proper name referring to an Arabian patriarch, a son of Eber and descendant of Shem. The top translations—'was Joktan,' 'And Joktan,' and 'of Joktan'—demonstrate its consistent role as a personal name connected to genealogical records. This consistency reveals the name's function primarily as a marker of lineage and tribal identity within the biblical narrative.
theologicalSignificance: Understanding Yoqṭân's root meaning of 'smallness' invites reflection on God's sovereign use of humble origins to fulfill His purposes, as seen in the lineage of nations descending from Shem. The patriarch Joktan, though his name suggests diminishment, is the progenitor of various Arabian tribes, illustrating how God can bring prominence and blessing from seemingly insignificant beginnings. This aligns with the biblical theme that God exalts the lowly and works through ordinary human history to accomplish divine plans, reminding believers to trust in God's power over human status or stature.
keyVerseReflection: Genesis 10:25 records that Eber had two sons, Peleg and Joktan, noting that 'in his days was the earth divided.' The mention of Joktan here situates him as a significant figure in the unfolding history of nations. The name's meaning, linked to smallness, contrasts with the earth's division during Peleg's time, suggesting that even those with humble names or origins have a vital role in God's providential ordering of the world. Joktan's presence in this genealogical context underscores God's sovereign orchestration of history through chosen lineages.
